I farm only 5 mu, so I keep things simple, practical, and timed to the wheat-maize rotation I already know well. I will plant winter wheat on all 5 mu, then after harvest I will put the same 5 mu into summer maize. Because some people in my family work off-farm, I do not want a management plan that is too labor-heavy or risky. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage to keep the crop stable, especially at key growth stages, instead of depending only on rainfall. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because on a small farm I care more about steady yield than saving seed. I will apply moderate fertilizer, not the highest amount, because I want good output but also need to control cost. I will use rotary tillage because it is faster and fits my scale better than deep ploughing every season. I will spray only as needed for common weeds, insects, and diseases, keeping the number of applications limited but enough to protect yield. My goal this year is stable production, manageable labor, and reliable grain from both crops.
